title: Each acts by his own nature. Your Lord knows who is guided.
subtitle: Your way shows what is inside you
then: Ibn 'Abbas said shakilah means {idea}his inclinations{/idea}. Mujahid said his inclinations and nature, Qatadah said his intentions, Ibn Zayd said his religion. Ibn Kathir reads it as a warning to the idolaters: {trap}everyone will be repaid for their deeds{/trap}, for nothing is hidden from Allah.
now: Your habits tell the story of your heart. What you do when no one is watching, what you spend your evenings on. {idea}Your actions grow from what is inside.{/idea} And only Allah sees the full picture, yours and everyone else's.
old: I can tell exactly who is right and who is wrong around me.
new: My deeds come from what is inside me, and only Allah truly knows who is guided.
try: Look at how you spent last evening. Ask what it says about what you love.

title: The soul belongs to my Lord's affair. Your knowledge is little.
subtitle: Humility before the unknown
then: Ibn Mas'ud narrated that while walking with the Prophet ﷺ, some People of the Book asked him about the soul. He fell silent and {idea}received revelation{/idea}, then recited this verse. 'Ikrimah reported that whatever knowledge you are given {reward}is great if it saves you from the Fire{/reward}, but next to Allah's knowledge it is very little.
now: You read articles on consciousness late at night. Brain scans, theories, podcasts. Still no one can tell you what you actually are. {idea}The verse is honest about that.{/idea} Keep learning, and stay humble about how much you know.
old: Given enough time, humans will understand everything.
new: Some things belong to Allah alone, and my knowledge is a small gift.
try: Next time you learn something new, say alhamdulillah for the little knowledge you have been given.

title: If He willed, He could take back what He revealed.
subtitle: The Quran is a gift that could be withdrawn
then: Ibn Kathir says this verse reminds of the great blessing of the Quran. Ibn Mas'ud said that at the end of time {trap}a wind will come and nothing will be left in a person's mushaf or heart, not even one verse{/trap}, and he recited this verse.
now: The mushaf on your shelf. The app on your phone. The surahs you learned as a child. {idea}You assume they will always be there.{/idea} What you have memorized and lived by is the part that stays with you.
old: The Quran will always be there whenever I get around to it.
new: The Quran is a gift I could lose, so I hold it close now.
try: Review one surah you memorized as a child, so it stays fresh in your heart.

title: It stays only as mercy, and His favor on you is great.
subtitle: Why the Quran is still with us
then: Right after saying He could take it away, Allah says it remains {reward}as a mercy from your Lord{/reward}. Ibn Kathir describes the Quran as {idea}the Book falsehood cannot reach{/idea}, sent by the All-Wise, a bounty on His servant and Messenger ﷺ.
now: You hear a child reciting at the masjid, or a voice on the radio in a taxi. {reward}Every recitation you hear is mercy still flowing.{/reward} It did not have to stay. It stays because He is kind.
old: Having the Quran is just a normal fact of my life.
new: That the Quran is still with me is a daily mercy.
try: Before you read Quran today, pause and thank Allah that it is still in your hands.

title: All humans and jinn together could not produce its like.
subtitle: The open challenge
then: Ibn Kathir says even if all humans and jinn came together and helped one another, {idea}they could never produce anything like it{/idea}. How could the words of created beings be like {idea}the words of the Creator, who has no equal{/idea}?
now: You have read thousands of books, captions, articles, messages. Most you forgot in a day. {idea}This one has been recited daily for over fourteen centuries.{/idea} Next time you read it, notice it is not like anything else you read.
old: The Quran is a great book among many great books.
new: The Quran is the speech of Allah, and nothing written can match it.
try: Read one short surah aloud slowly today and listen to it as Allah's own words.

title: Every kind of example given, yet most refused.
subtitle: When proof is not the problem
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Allah {idea}furnished them with evidence and definitive proof{/idea} and explained the truth in detail. Despite that, {trap}most people insisted on denying and rejecting it{/trap}.
now: You keep saying you need one more lecture, one more book, one more sign before you change. {idea}You already have plenty.{/idea} Maybe the next step is not more information but one small act.
old: Once I have enough proof, I will change.
new: The proof is already here. What I need is the will to act on it.
try: Pick one thing you already know you should do. Do it today, without waiting for more proof.

title: Make a spring gush from the ground, then we will believe.
subtitle: The list of demands begins
then: Ibn Ishaq narrated that the leaders of Quraysh gathered behind the Ka'bah and sent for the Prophet ﷺ. He came quickly, {reward}hoping they would be guided{/reward}. They offered him wealth, leadership, even kingship. He refused all of it: {idea}Allah has sent me as a messenger, to bring good news and a warning{/idea}. Then the demands began.
now: You tell Allah: give me the job and I will pray on time. Heal my mother and I will wear hijab. Fix my marriage, then I will start reading Quran. {trap}Faith on condition.{/trap} He is not a vending machine. He already gave you the message.
old: If Allah gives me what I ask for, then I will commit.
new: Faith is not a deal I make with Allah after He pays up first.
try: Start one good habit today that you had been saving until Allah gives you something.

title: Or a garden of palms and grapes with rivers flowing.
subtitle: Asking for luxury as proof
then: They told the Prophet ﷺ their land was small and their life hard, and asked him to {trap}move the mountains away and make rivers flow like those of Syria and Iraq{/trap}. He replied: {idea}I was not sent for this{/idea}. If you accept what I brought, it is your good fortune in this world and the next.
now: You judge whether someone's advice is worth hearing by their car, their house, their followers. {trap}A rich person must be right.{/trap} The truth does not need a garden to prove it.
old: Success and wealth are signs that someone is on the right path.
new: Truth stands on its own, with or without a garden around it.
try: Listen today to someone wise who has little money, and take their advice seriously.

title: Or bring the sky down on us, or bring Allah and angels.
subtitle: Demands that dared punishment
then: When they demanded that the sky fall on them, the Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}that is for Allah to decide; if He wills, He will do it{/idea}. One of them said they would never believe until he brought Allah and the angels before them. {trap}When they said this, the Prophet ﷺ got up and left them.{/trap}
now: Some arguments you cannot win, because the other side is not looking for an answer. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ stood up and left.{/idea} You can too, calmly, when a debate online or at dinner becomes mockery.
old: I have to keep arguing until the other person admits I am right.
new: When someone only wants to mock, I can walk away calmly and leave it to Allah.
try: Next time a conversation about faith turns mocking, end it politely and make dua for them.

title: Glory be to my Lord. Am I anything but a human messenger?
subtitle: The humble answer to impossible demands
then: They said even if he climbed into the sky, {trap}we will not believe until you bring down a book we can read{/trap}. They also asked him for palaces of gold, so he would not need to seek provision in the markets like them. His answer begins with {idea}glory be to my Lord{/idea}, then: I am only a human sent as a messenger.
now: People expect you to be perfect because you pray. Or you expect it of your imam, your parents, yourself. {idea}Even the best of creation said: I am a human.{/idea} He was honest about it, and still did his job fully.
old: A person of faith should have answers and powers for everything.
new: Being human is not a flaw in faith. Conveying the truth honestly is the job.
try: When someone asks a question you cannot answer today, say I do not know, with no shame.

title: What stopped them was: has Allah sent a human?
subtitle: The oldest excuse
then: Ibn Kathir says most people {trap}found it strange that a human would be sent as a messenger{/trap}. He cites how Fir'awn's people and earlier nations said the same: you are only humans like us. But it is a mercy, he explains: {reward}a messenger of their own kind, whom they can understand and learn from directly{/reward}.
now: You hear good advice from your little brother, a younger colleague, a convert who has been Muslim for a year. Your first thought: who are you to tell me? {trap}The messenger looked too ordinary.{/trap} Same pattern.
old: I only take guidance from people who are clearly above me.
new: Guidance often comes through ordinary people, and that is a mercy.
try: Thank someone younger or less experienced than you for something useful they told you.

title: If angels walked the earth, an angel would be their messenger.
subtitle: A messenger of your own kind
then: Ibn Kathir explains that if angels lived on earth as humans do, {idea}they would have been sent an angel of their own kind{/idea}. Since you are human, Allah sent messengers from among yourselves, {reward}as a kindness and a mercy{/reward}, so they could be spoken to face to face.
now: Quraysh mocked the Prophet ﷺ for walking in the markets seeking provision like everyone else. {reward}That is exactly why you can follow him.{/reward} An angel could not show you how to be patient with a crying baby or a hard boss.
old: The Prophet ﷺ was so far above us that I cannot really follow him.
new: He was sent as a human so I could follow him in my own human life.
try: Learn one small thing the Prophet ﷺ did at home, and do it today.

title: Allah is enough as a witness between me and you.
subtitle: When you have said what you can
then: After all the demands, the Prophet ﷺ is told to end with this. Ibn Kathir explains: {idea}Allah is a witness over me and over you. He knows what I have brought.{/idea} If I were lying, He would deal with me. He knows {idea}who deserves guidance{/idea}.
now: Your relatives misread your intentions. Your manager does not believe your side. You have explained three times. {idea}At some point, you can stop.{/idea} Allah saw what happened. That is enough.
old: If people do not believe me, I have to keep proving myself.
new: When I have spoken the truth, Allah is enough as my witness.
try: Think of one misunderstanding you cannot fix. Say: Allah is enough as a witness, and let it rest.

title: Whom Allah guides is truly guided.
subtitle: Guidance is in His hands, so ask Him for it
then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}whomever Allah guides cannot be led astray{/idea}. Those who ignored the truth will be gathered blind, mute and deaf, {trap}as they were to the truth in this world{/trap}, at the moment they need those senses most. The Prophet ﷺ said the One who made them walk on their feet can make them walk on their faces.
now: Your eyes, your ears, your tongue. You use them all day for the screen, the gossip, the playlist. {idea}They were given to find the truth.{/idea} Using them for that now is how you keep them.
old: I can find my own way. Guidance is something I figure out myself.
new: Guidance is from Allah, so I ask for it and use my senses to follow it.
try: In every rak'ah today, say ihdina as-sirat al-mustaqim slowly and mean it.
